description: Evaluation cases for the cketh skill. Tests token discovery via the minter, the deposit-address flow (deposit_erc20 / deposit_eth), helper-contract argument encoding, and the two-ledger approval needed for ckERC20 withdrawals.

output_evals.name: Discover supported ckERC20 tokens at runtime
output_evals.prompt: In TypeScript, how do I get the list of ckERC20 tokens (symbol, ERC-20 contract, ledger canister id) that can currently be deposited on mainnet? Just the function, no UI, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Calls get_minter_info on the ckETH minter sv3dd-oaaaa-aaaar-qacoa-cai
Reads supported_ckerc20_tokens (ckerc20_token_symbol, erc20_contract_address, ledger_canister_id) rather than hardcoding a token list
Does NOT treat the orchestrator or a static table as the authoritative list of depositable tokens

output_evals.name: USDT from a centralized exchange uses deposit_erc20
output_evals.prompt: My users hold USDT on Binance and want ckUSDT in my ICP app. Binance can only send a plain transfer to an address. Which ckETH minter call gives them the address to send to, and what are its arguments? Just the call and a short explanation, no full app.
expected_behaviors: Uses the deposit_erc20 endpoint on the ckETH minter with erc20_contract_address set to the USDT contract and mode = Unsponsored { subaccount }
Explains the address is credited to the caller's principal plus subaccount (there is no owner argument), so it must be called with the user's identity or by the custodial canister
Mentions the 24 hour scanning window / re-calling deposit_erc20 to re-arm, or the per-token minimum_deposit_amount
States that only Ethereum L1 transfers are credited (not Arbitrum/Base/BSC)

output_evals.name: Helper contract arguments for depositErc20
output_evals.prompt: I'm calling depositErc20 on the ckETH helper contract from viem. How exactly do I encode the principal and subaccount arguments, and what must happen before this call? Short answer with a code snippet, no backend code.
expected_behaviors: Encodes the principal as bytes32: length byte followed by principal bytes, zero-padded (e.g. encodePrincipalToEthAddress from @icp-sdk/canisters/cketh)
Encodes the subaccount as 32 bytes (zeros for the default account)
Requires an ERC-20 approve of the helper contract address before depositErc20
Reads the helper address from get_minter_info deposit_with_subaccount_helper_contract_address instead of the legacy smart_contract_address

output_evals.name: ckUSDC withdrawal needs ckETH approval
output_evals.prompt: List the canister calls, in order, to withdraw 100 ckUSDC to an Ethereum address from a user's own account. Just the ordered list of calls with canister ids, no code.
expected_behaviors: Approves the ckETH minter as spender on the ckETH ledger (ss2fx-dyaaa-aaaar-qacoq-cai) for the gas fee, sized from eip_1559_transaction_price with the ckUSDC ledger id
Approves the ckETH minter as spender on the ckUSDC ledger (xevnm-gaaaa-aaaar-qafnq-cai) for the amount (100_000_000 with 6 decimals)
Calls withdraw_erc20 on the minter (not withdraw_eth) with ckerc20_ledger_id, recipient and amount
Notes the user must hold ckETH to pay gas

trigger_evals.description: Queries to test whether the skill activates correctly. 'should_trigger' queries should cause the skill to load; 'should_not_trigger' queries should NOT activate this skill.
should_trigger: How do I let users deposit USDC from Ethereum into my ICP app as ckUSDC?
Withdraw ckETH back to a MetaMask address from my canister
Which ERC-20 tokens are supported as ckERC20 and how do I find their ledger canisters?
Give each user an Ethereum deposit address for ckUSDT
should_not_trigger: How do I transfer ckUSDC between two ICP principals?
Call an Ethereum smart contract's view function from my Rust canister
